messages.content: Threat-model an autonomous coding harness acceptance contract. Demand machine-checkable invariants and return only contracted JSON.

We need to prevent an implementation agent from authoring the test oracle that qualifies its own patch. Proposed two-supplier lifecycle: (1) acceptance supplier returns test bytes from exact context and structured given/when/then/forbidden vectors; host injects into an isolated incumbent snapshot, demands a failing red witness, procures per-vector independent reviews, and stores immutable bytes/digests/command/reviews as a dated capsule; (2) implementation suppliers receive the capsule tests in isolated copies, but capsule paths are outside writablePaths. Host runs them after every edit, rejects any digest change, integrates source only after protected-border checks, then copies post-integration authoritative source to a new workspace, reinjects the exact capsule, and reruns it. Promotion requires this protected post-integration witness. Acceptance capsules never land in the authoritative source merely to make it red.

The observed bad incumbent wrote a test containing every vector id but omitted several operations and forbidden assertions; ordinary tests passed and semantic reviewers initially said yes. Threat-model capsule substitution, stale snapshots, red tests that fail for irrelevant reasons, tests that always fail, supplier collusion, command/path escapes, artifact imports, hidden network/time dependence, and post-integration replay. State exact mechanisms and tests needed before implementation.

completion.text:
{
  "verdict": "sound-with-required-changes",
  "strengths": [
    "Separation of concerns between the acceptance supplier and the implementation supplier breaks self-certification loops.",
    "Immutable capsule storage prevents tampering with the test oracle post-generation.",
    "Requirement for post-integration red witness ensures test integrity persists across source code evolution.",
    "Hard restriction of capsule paths outside writablePaths minimizes attack surface for path injection.",
    "Structured vector enforcement mandates complete coverage of forbidden and required assertions."
  ],
  "risks": [
    "Test flakes or environment dependence could lead to perpetual red witnesses that halt the pipeline.",
    "Time or network-dependent tests allow collusion by introducing environmental triggers.",
    "Symbolic link attacks or path traversal in non-authoritative workspaces could bridge isolation boundaries.",
    "Stale snapshot usage might cause tests to pass in an outdated context, bypassing logic changes.",
    "Insufficient sandboxing of artifact imports allows malicious payloads to execute during test instantiation."
  ],
  "requiredMechanisms": [
    "Mandatory content-addressable storage for capsules verified by SHA-256 hashes.",
    "Strict hardware-level process isolation using Linux Namespaces or gVisor for every test run.",
    "Compulsory mocking of system clock and network stack within the test container to ensure determinism.",
    "Hardware-enforced read-only mounting of capsule storage volumes for implementation agents.",
    "Automated diffing of binary artifacts post-test to detect hidden side-channel modifications.",
    "Mandatory signed attestations from independent reviewers for each individual vector prior to capsule sealing.",
    "Initialization of fresh ephemeral filesystem snapshots for every test execution iteration."
  ],
  "badIncumbentTests": [
    "A test suite that reports a 100% success rate while containing empty loop bodies or missing critical logic assertions for stated vectors.",
    "A test suite that dynamically generates its own assertion logic based on external environment variables rather than static capsule input.",
    "A test suite that utilizes non-deterministic wait states or sleep timers to obscure race conditions.",
    "A test suite that makes undocumented external network calls to resolve its own 'success' criteria."
  ]
}
